newsitem.title: UK: London stocks hit record, dollar rallies.
newsitem.headline: London stocks hit record, dollar rallies.

text.p: The dollar rallied on Wednesday despite mixed signals from the German Bundesbank, while the London stock exchange led a clutch of European bourses to record levels.

The London, Copenhagen, Stockholm, Amsterdam and Zurich stock markets all hit new highs, but the French and German bourses stayed away from the party as Wall Street failed to follow through on its strong performance on Tuesday.

The Dow Industrials Average was off its lows but still showing an eight point loss as the London markets closed. Traders said the Dow was dragged down by weaker bonds that appeared to have ignored favourable prices data for January.

"It looks like the stock market is still digesting its gains from last week. It is in a holding pattern and under no great selling pressure," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.
The dollar closed higher, taking a larger-than-expected U.S. trade gap in its stride and digesting conflicting comments from the German Bundesbank.

The U.S. currency eroded some of its morning gains on news that the country's trade deficit rose to $10.29 billion in December from a revised $7.94 billion in November. The consumer price index rose just 0.1 percent on the month, less than the 0.3 percent increase expected.

"The U.S. data showed a largely as expected deterioration in the trade position and further evidence of the subdued nature of inflation," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser at Bank of America in London. "This should tend to support the asset markets and leave the dollar little changed."

The German central bank's monthly report and remarks from its chief Hans Tietmeyer earlier weighed on the dollar, but the currency was later helped by Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke who was quoted as saying a dollar level of 1.70 to 1.75 marks would not risk importing inflation into Germany.
The dollar ended in Europe at 1.6961 marks, off a session low of 1.6806 and up from late Tuesday's European level of 1.6904. Against the yen it was at 124.23, down from 123.94.
A bigger-than-expected increase in British retail sales catapulted sterling higher, helping it recoup much of Tuesday's five-pfennig loss.
The Italian lira had a rocky ride once more, however, falling to a three-month low near 1,000 per mark in early trade before recovering to 995.80.
It was helped by Prime Minister Romano Prodi's announcement of a mini-budget which he said would enable Italy to meet the criteria for monetary union.
The London stock market scaled new heights as investors shrugged off the pullback on Wall Street and the jump in retail sales that could point to a rise in interest rates.
The blue chip FTSE 100 index added 25.1 points to close at its intraday high of 4,357.4. Advancers beat decliners 57 to 36.

Bank stocks were in focus again after Goldman Sachs downgraded Barclays shares following results at the low end of expectations. Barclays ended down another 15.5 pence at 11.13 pounds after dropping 70-1/2p on Tuesday.

B.A.T Industries rose 18.5p to 546.5 after a surge in U.S. tobacco stocks amid renewed hopes that the industry is taking steps to settle its litigation problems, although B.A.T played down the reports.
German shares ended bourse trade sharply lower and slid further in later electronic dealing. The 30-share DAX index ended down 42.41 points, or 1.29 percent, at 3,233.75
The IBIS DAX index of screen-based trade ended 21 points lower at 3,209 points as market jitters in advance of Friday's options expiry and Wall Street's weak opening combined to drag the index down.

"The downward pressure is coming more from the derivatives side than the retail side because of the expiry and this makes people more nervous. With futures traders things tend to move quickly, hence the rapid pace of change," one trader said.
French shares ended 0.9 percent lower as investors opted to take profits on fears the market might pull back from such high levels.
"This downturn is normal. We're at levels where people start getting worried," one trader said.
"The market needs to breathe before resuming its upward move. That's why the good U.S. figures didn't really help," said another.
The blue-chip CAC 40 index finished down 22.76 points at 2,594.76 while the CAC-40 futures contract was down 1.0 point at 2,607.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6961 marks and 124.22 yen compared with 1.6904 marks and 123.94 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS - CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 25.1 points, or 0.58 percent, at 4,357.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 ended down 22.76 points, or 0.87 percent, at 2,594.76.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended down 42.41 points, or 1.29 percent, at 3,233.75. In later screen-based trade the IBIS-DAX index closed down 21.79 at 3,209.04.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $346.55, up 95 cents from Tuesday. Silver finished at $5.19, down five cents.
